title: Prepare work sites for fumigation interventions

lessons.title: Site preparation and securing the area
lessons.html:
The stakes are high

Fumigant gases can kill quickly and travel through gaps, ducts, drains, conveyors and adjoining rooms. Preparing the site is the step that keeps people alive. It must follow the fumigation management plan and the label, and only persons registered for fumigation, or trained workers under their direct supervision as permitted, may carry it out.

Confirm the plan on site

  1. Walk the site with the client contact and the fumigation team leader.
  2. Confirm the structure, bins or stacks to be fumigated and the volume or tonnage.
  3. Identify all connections through which gas could escape: conveyors, elevator legs, aeration ducts, tunnels, drains, cable trenches, shared roof spaces, adjoining offices and houses.
  4. Mark out the exclusion zone required by the plan and identify where people normally work or live nearby.

Clearing people and animals

  • Inform all occupants, workers and neighbours who may be affected, as required, with the date, time and duration.
  • Evacuate the structure and exclusion zone of all people, livestock, pets and working dogs.
  • Remove items the label requires to be removed, such as food not being treated, medicines, plants or sensitive equipment.
  • Isolate electrical equipment and switch off ignition sources and pilot lights as the label requires.

Securing the area

  • Post fumigation warning signs at every entrance and around the perimeter. Signs typically show the fumigant name, the skull and crossbones, date and time of application, the fumigator's name and emergency contact, and the statement that entry is prohibited. Use languages understood by people on and around the site.
  • Lock doors and gates and arrange guarding or patrols for the duration.
  • Inform site security, the control room and shift supervisors.
  • Isolate interconnecting conveyors and equipment by lockout so they cannot be started during fumigation.

The final occupancy check

Immediately before fumigant is introduced, two people check every room, roof void, bin top, tunnel and toilet to confirm that nobody is inside. Record the check, the time and the names of the people who did it.

lessons.title: Sealing, equipment and readiness
lessons.html:
Sealing for gas-tightness

The fumigation succeeds only if the gas is held. Sealing is painstaking work.

SituationSealing actions
Rooms and buildingsTape or seal windows, doors, vents, eaves, pipe and cable penetrations; seal drains; or cover the whole building with gas-proof tarpaulins
Silo binsSeal top hatches, inspection doors, spouts, bottom slides and aeration fan openings; check for cracks
Bag stacksLay gas-proof floor sheets if needed, cover the stack, overlap and seal joins, weight edges with sand snakes
ContainersSeal door gaps and vents as the procedure requires

Inspect sheets for holes and tears before use and repair them. Where possible, pressure-test sealed bins or enclosures before fumigation.

Preparing monitoring points

Install gas sampling lines to planned points inside the structure, for example at the top, middle and bottom of a bin, before sealing. Label each line and lead it to a safe sampling position outside the exclusion zone. Identify perimeter monitoring points near occupied areas.

Equipment and PPE check

  • Fumigant product in the correct quantity, calculated and verified.
  • Applicators, probes or dispensers as required.
  • Gas monitoring instruments, charged and checked; detector tubes in date.
  • Respiratory protection specified by the label: full-face respirators with the correct canisters within their service life, or self-contained breathing apparatus, fit tested.
  • Gloves as the label specifies, overalls and boots.
  • First aid kit, emergency water, label, SDS and emergency contact numbers.
  • Means of communication between team members.

Pre-application briefing

The team leader confirms roles: applicators, standby person, gas monitor operator, perimeter guard. Review emergency procedures, including what to do if gas is detected outside the zone, if someone feels unwell, or if a person is found inside. Confirm the sequence of application and exit route. Only proceed when every item on the readiness checklist is complete. Hands-on first aid training by an accredited provider is required for the team.

Key points

  • Identify every route by which gas could escape, including conveyors, ducts, drains and adjoining spaces.
  • Evacuate people and animals, notify those affected and post multilingual warning signs.
  • Lock out interconnected equipment and secure the site for the full duration.
  • Seal thoroughly, install labelled sampling lines and check sheets for damage.
  • Perform a two-person occupancy check and readiness briefing before application.

quiz.question: Which of these could allow fumigant gas to escape a silo bin into work areas?
When should gas sampling lines be installed?

options.text: Only if a leak is suspected

quiz.question: Who should carry out the final occupancy check?

options.text: Nobody; the evacuation notice is enough
Two people, checking every space and recording it

quiz.question: What should be done with interconnecting conveyors during fumigation?

options.text: Run them to circulate gas into offices
Isolate them by lockout so they cannot start

quiz.question: Which information do fumigation warning signs typically show?

options.text: Fumigant name, skull and crossbones, date and time, and emergency contact
